This is an issue that keeps arising, but STEAM has been of little help. The Community members are great with offering troubleshooting tips, but unfortunately they are isolated cases that work some but not all. That said, STEAM sells older products that seem tend to play well the first time and then cause black screen on startup from that point forward. That is the case here. SEGA customer service does not support it anymore, or so I'm told, and STEAM refused a refund. So, $25 later and I have a game sitting my library I can't play. 

This is also after running as adminsrator, verifying files, changing resolutions, uninstall/reinstall, etc. But why even sell things that require that much "troubleshooting" to make work.

Sadly, this game's been utterly abandoned. Anyone looking to build up their abilities and customize their Astartes for Multiplayer Mode are going to be SOL, unless they have buddies to commit to private games.

Space Marine is one of the only Warhammer games other than DoW to break the 40k curse. While there are other decent entries into 40k's growing video game lineup, most suffer from a somewhat cliche storyline, or mediocre game mechanics.

First off, the fact you play as Ultramarines might throw some off from even giving this game the time of day, but I'm telling you now that Captain Titus is the most badass Ultramarine you can play as. You land on a forge world in the beginning of the campaign in response to an ork invasion and to retake a captured manufactorum holding a Warlord class titan. 

The gameplay you're treated to is a mix of a 3rd person shooter and hack'n'slash, and the game handles it very well. Ranged weapons have solid sound design and hit with the impact you'd expect from a fully automatic .75 caliber rocket launcher, and melee weapons all have the weight behind them to back up the power that you force onto your unwilling Xenos test subjects. It's gritty, bloody, gory, and oh so satisfying. Refill your health by brutally executing your enemies, and the amount of health you gain back is directly tied to how big the enemy is, just make sure you're not getting swarmed when executing because enemies will still attack you. As for difficulty, the game itself is not excrutiatingly difficult on hard, but it does provide a healthy challenge and makes you change your tactics dependent on what mistake you made last try. Enemies will hit harder and be more aggressive on higher difficulties, much akin to how Orks really are.

After you finish the about 8-10 hour campaign, you can take the fight online, although not so much anymore. Right now the only mode you'll find populated is Sieze Ground which is basically Conquest from Battlefield, but there's enough players to make matches, even though you'll likely see the same group of players almost every time. Matches are 8v8 with Space Marines vs Chaos Space Marines, and you can customize your character by either using a pre-made chapter color scheme, a pre-made chapter oriented set of armor, or you can make your own with a massive array of armor pieces, colors, emblems, and trimmings to make a massive 1.8 billion possibilities. You can customize your classes with weapons and perks, including weapon specific perks you achieve by using whichever weapon of your choice (bolter with kraken/targeter OP). There are 3 distinct classes in Multiplayer, the all-around tactical, the melee oriented Assault with a jump pack, and the heavy weapon specialist Devastators. Each class has a couple unique traits to help with their playstyle. Tactical has the fastest sprint speed with normal shields, Assault has weaker shields in exchange for increased mobility with its jump pack, and Devastators have the strongest shields to help compensate for their slow movement speed. When there is a good group of players in a game, it can be a helluva lot of fun, but sadly the multiplayer is mostly dead right now. 

Space Marine is possibly the best shooter in 40k's lineup and is very fun to play. The campaign, while not stellar, is certainly worth playing through the end. Although if you want this for multiplayer, I'd have to give it a pass unless you have a clan or something to play with.
